_comment: Per-artwork creation-date corrections, keyed by objectKey (folder/filename, NFC-normalised). Applied by build-data.mjs after extractYear, so it overrides whatever normalize-metadata.mjs derived. This file exists because the derived year is not durable: normalize-metadata.mjs recomputes entry.year on every run, and fetch-wikimedia-metadata.mjs spawns it after every scrape, so a correction written into a sidecar is reverted by the next ingest. Corrections belong here instead. 'year' is the integer the catalogue sorts and shelves by; 'dateString' is how the source words it, shown on the detail page. Every entry cites the page it came from in _why. Never enter a date you have not read on Commons, Wikidata, or the holding institution's own catalogue. Regenerate data with 'pnpm assets:build-data' after editing.

_why.collection-of-beauty/Albrecht_Dürer_-_De: The Albertina, which holds the sheet (Inv. 4840), dates it "um 1500" — around 1500, not 1500. Its record explicitly addresses the "1512" written on the sheet: that inscription is treated not as a dating but as evidence of a later inventory revision by Dürer himself. Wikidata Q21151884 carries both 1500 (preferred rank) and 1512 as P571 values, and the Commons file page surfaces only the 1512 inscription with the note that it is probably by a later hand. So the integer 1500 is the right representative, but it is a circa, not a documented year of execution — the filename's own "(ca. 1500)" is more honest than the catalogue's bare 1500. Source: https://sammlungenonline.albertina.at/objects/40278. Independently re-checked: SURVIVES. I read the Albertina record myself: 'Der Flügel einer Blauracke', Dürer, Inv. 4840, dated 'um 1500'. It says the '1512' inscription is not a date of execution but, if authentic at all, evidence of a later stock audit. The Commons file page is the same object: Albertina, accession 4840, Wikidata Q21151884, date 'circa 1500', inscription 1512 'probably by later hand'. The year fits Dürer's lifespan (1471-1528). A circa, not a precise year.

_why.collection-of-beauty/Claude_Monet_-_Vase: The Commons file page has no institution, no accession and no Wikidata link; its date is {{otherdate|by|1926}} and its Flickr source URL is dead (404). "by 1926" is a terminus-ante-quem derived from Monet's death year, exactly the lifespan-leak pattern. I identified the painting instead: the Commons Artwork template records it as signed "Claude Monet" lower right, and Commons also holds File:Vase de tulipes (1885) Claude Monet (W 942).jpg. I downloaded 500px renderings of both and compared them — same composition, same tulip count and arrangement, same green-glass tapered vase, same signature in the lower right; they are the same painting. That file's description cites Wildenstein 1996 vol. II no. 942 and Sotheby's Impressionist & Modern Evening, New York, 2006, lot 8. I then read the Sotheby's lot page itself: Claude Monet, "Vase de tulipes", 1885, oil on canvas, 50.3 × 37.5 cm, signed lower right, Wildenstein no. 942. Dimensions and signature position both match. Source: https://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2006/impressionist-modern-art-evening-n08239/lot.8.html. Independently re-checked: SURVIVES. The Sotheby's lot page loads: Claude Monet, 'Vase de tulipes', oil on canvas, 50.3 x 37.5 cm, signed 'Claude Monet' lower right, Wildenstein 942. The researcher said the heading reads '1885', but my fetch did not reproduce that. The catalogue note does settle the date: most of the Durand-Ruel door panels were done by 1884, and 'the present work was not finished until 1885'. To check it is the same object, I pulled 500px renderings of the flagged file and of File:Vase de tulipes (1885) Claude Monet (W 942).jpg. They are the same painting: same tulips and arrangement, same tapered green vase, same signature placement. The flagged file's aspect ratio (768x1029 = 0.746) matches the lot's 50.3x37.5 cm (0.746). The Commons flagged file itself says only {{otherdate|by|1926}}, which is Monet's death year used as an end limit. 1885 is inside his life (1840-1926).

Independently re-checked: SURVIVES. I checked the same object on the candidate's own Commons page. Its Date field reads "Unknown date, but author died in 1904. It is believed that the portrait was painted around the date that the author married the subject, 1864". The same page gives National Portrait Gallery, NPG 5048, wikidata Q28050210. The pipeline took 1904 from that sentence, and 1904 is Watts's death year. The cited Wikidata item is labelled "Ellen Terry ('Choosing')" by G. F. Watts, NPG collection, inventory NPG 5048. Its P571 is 1864 at year precision, and the fetch showed no circa qualifier. 1864 falls within Watts's 1817-1904 lifespan. Caveat: the NPG page returned HTTP 403, so I could not read the museum's own wording. The Commons prose is hedged ('believed', 'around'), which is why the Wikidata statement carries this change.
